THE PLAYER’S HANDBOOK · CUSTOM RULES

Eleven a side.
A new kind of tactics.

This is our custom Football Chess variation: a 12 × 15 pitch, four-square goals, and eleven footballers per side. Each team has one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and three pawns.

01 · Shape the play

The attacker positions their team, the defender responds, then the attacker kicks. Each positioning turn includes one regular move and one free pawn move, in either order. End the turn to leave any unused moves behind.

02 · Move like chess

Use chess movement patterns, with a maximum of ten squares per move. Pieces block movement; knights jump over them, including while dribbling. Pawns can move one square forward, backward, left, or right.

03 · Keep the ball moving

Kicks follow the carrier’s kicking directions. A short pass stops at the first piece in its path; an empty target leaves a loose ball. A friendly back-pass to the king requires an immediate kick: the king cannot hold or dribble it.

04 · Pick your finish

Aim at any legal goal target in files e–h. The shooter commits the target, then the defending king may move one legal square or hold before the shot resolves. Only kings can enter the four-by-two goal boxes.

A finish depends on the whole shot

Closer shots give the keeper less time to react. A tighter shooting angle makes the target harder to hit. The keeper’s position matters along the actual shot path, from the shooter to the chosen goal target: a shot travelling farther from the keeper is harder to save.

The model combines the chance of hitting the target with the chance of beating the keeper. A longer flight lets the keeper cover more ground. Kings have their full saving reach inside their own four-by-two box; outside it, they can only make a weaker block. The blue reach area and dashed coverage line show this geometry during a shot preview.

After the defending king’s one-square reaction or decision to hold, a shot can score, be saved, or go wide. A save gives the keeper ordinary possession. A wide shot gives the defending king an immediate goal kick; a king outside the box returns to a free square in their own box first. Goal targets display the current chance of scoring, and the reaction panel shows all three outcome probabilities.

Passing accuracy

Passes up to ten squares have 100% accuracy. Beyond ten squares, accuracy falls by ten percentage points per additional square, to a minimum of 25%. Target previews show the current odds before you kick.

Tackles, pawns, and knights

A piece that can reach the opposing carrier using its capture pattern may tackle: choose a highlighted landing square beside the carrier. Both footballers stay on the pitch. Tackles against a knight succeed 50% of the time; other legal tackles succeed 100%. The defender moves to the chosen adjacent square either way. A failed tackle leaves the knight with the ball and consumes the defender’s regular move. Pawn tackles remain forward-diagonal. A free pawn move only repositions the pawn and cannot tackle. Knights can still jump over defenders while dribbling.

Computer difficulty

Casual chooses actions using immediate positional and scoring heuristics. Tactical looks ahead at your replies and weighs the expected outcomes of shots, passes, and risky tackles. Both levels use the same rules and scoring odds. Opponent pace controls the pause between actions independently of difficulty. You can change either setting during a match.

Match conventions

Pieces are never captured. There is no check, castling, en passant, or pawn promotion. Knights kick with one L-shaped jump; other kicks follow their movement directions. Turnovers restart the sequence for the new attacking team. A goal resets the formation and gives kickoff to the conceding side. Most goals at full time wins; the clock stops when paused.

Model notes

This is a custom game heuristic, tuned for play rather than calibrated to real match data or a published expected-goals fit. Shooting distance, angle, goalkeeper position, and trajectory inform its design; the probability formula and coefficients are our own.

Background: Goalkeeper positioning research ↗ · StatsBomb expected-goals factors ↗

The shot-model coefficients, goal-box dimensions, and long-pass accuracy curve are playable defaults for this custom variation and can be revised.
